findings.claim: Admissibility Idempotency-Key is admissibility:<case>:<criterion>:sha256(body) and is not bound to the If-Match version. The server fingerprint (rait-case-command.service.ts:763, command+actor+target+payload) also leaves out If-Match. The replay lookup (lines 773-786) runs before the version check (810-819) and returns the stored response for 24h. TriagePage.saveHumanCriteria re-sends all three criteria on every save. So after the first save, saving again with one corrected criterion replays each unchanged criterion: no write happens, the client gets a false success, and RaitHttp.postCommand (rait-http.ts:85) stores the stale replayed ETag. The next changed criterion then fails 412 under the stale ETag. An A->B->A edit also returns a 'true' success while the database still holds B. This breaks ADR-0041's claim that replay is bound to current persisted case versions, and contract §5 (sequential saves use the returned ETag). No sensor covers a re-save or a changed-then-reverted criterion.
findings.fix: Bind replay to the parent version. Add the If-Match value to the server request fingerprint (or key the stored replay by version) so a reused key under a different version cannot replay a stale result. Make the client key include the If-Match/version it sends, or otherwise avoid colliding with earlier versions. Add Inspector sensors (HTTP e2e and page wiring) for: save all three, change one, save again (expect 200 and a new version); and A->B->A (persisted verdict A, fresh ETag).

findings.claim: COMMAND_AUDIT_ROLES hardcodes 'rait-analyst' for triage and save-admissibility. The existing policy tuples allow both rait-analyst and rait-secretary for these (policy.ts 'rait-case' triage tuple; 'rait-admissibility' writers). audit.write therefore records role rait-analyst when a secretary performs the command, which is false audit attribution. Admit/reject are analyst-only, so the constant was correct only for those commands.
findings.fix: Record the authenticated actor's actual authorizing role (from principal/request context, intersected with the policy tuple) for triage and save-admissibility, and add an e2e assertion on the audit role for a secretary actor.
